responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the Matsushita/Panasonic MN10300 and AM33-family processors, including its GNU/Linux variant, and is responsible for turning GCC’s generic RTL into assembly and target decisions that match this architecture’s ISA, ABI, and processor-specific features. Its central header and option files define the architectural configuration, register set, calling convention, PIC and ABI defaults, CPU-selection switches, and Linux-specific toolchain/assembler conventions, while the machine-description, predicates, constraints, and condition-code mode files describe the instruction patterns, operand legality, scheduling/LIW forms, compare-and-branch behavior, and special CC modes used by the recognizer and scheduler. The implementation files provide the procedural target hooks that complement those descriptions: option override handling, operand/address printing, address and PIC legitimization, frame and prologue/epilogue logic, argument passing and returns, cost and register-class modeling, symbol/section details, and MN10300-specific RTL reorganization such as LIW bundling and AM33 low-overhead SETLB/Lcc loop formation. Overall, this module covers the full machine-dependent code-generation layer for MN10300-family systems, distinguishing it from generic RTL infrastructure by owning this target’s instruction selection, ABI behavior, assembly syntax, and late target-specific optimization/emission logic.
